title: Errementari
subtitle: /The Blacksmith and the Devil
review: For this film, the writers reconstructed an approximation of an extinct Basque dialect, from antique documents, and then trained the actors to speak it. It very cool attention to detail, and that makes it even funnier that Netflix offer it with the most horrendous American dub by default. There are some beautiful scenes filmed on location, but in many other ways it looks like a cheap streaming movie. The filmography, costumes and sets, have that TV movie feel. The camera doesn't move much, except when it's handheld. A lot of scenes use natural light, and interiors have very flat lighting. There are hardly any wide shots, and the whole thing just doesn't feel very cinematic or engaging. It's a shame that the passion that went into the writing and representation of this small area of Europe has been squandered on such cheap and plain production. I went back to the English dub after a while, to inject some comedy when it was starting to feel too dull. I feel like fairy tale adaptations are often a bit weak on character depth. I mean, we all know how Cinderella lived and what she did, but we don't think much about what her mannerisms or personality.
spoilers: Having said it looks cheap, they do go for a hell scene at the end. In the past I have said I wanted to see a low budget horror movie surprise me by allocating all the money to crazy hell transition at the end. Unfortunately the scene here isn't that interesting, and I still need the rest of the film to to be good, to be satisfied with this fantasy. Why are people in hell always flinching away from demon's pitchforks? Are they worried they'll die if the demons stab them?
